speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This provides for the standardisation of provisions relating to the international multimodal transport of goods to and from any ASEAN member country, under a multimodal transport contract.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: A harmonised transport system will enhance regional connectivity in ASEAN and facilitate the free movement of goods, services and investment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: To support this goal, ASEAN member states have signed three framework agreements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The ASEAN Framework Agreement on the Facilitation of Goods in Transit was signed in 1998, followed by the ASEAN Framework Agreement on Multimodal Transport in 2005.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The ASEAN Framework Agreement on the Facilitation of Inter-State Transport was signed in 2009.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: ASEAN member states have been ratifying these agreements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: After all ASEAN member states have ratified the agreement, it will provide a single, unified framework for the multimodal transport of goods within ASEAN.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This will include market access for Singapore logistics operators to operate in other ASEAN member states under a set of regionally aligned standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: These goods are carried by a multimodal transport operator registered with the Competent National Body established in the ASEAN member states, under a single multimodal transport contract where the origin or destination of the goods delivery is in an ASEAN member state.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: I will go through each of these areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: First, the Bill will put in place the legislative framework for Singapore to recognise the Competent National Body, established by each ASEAN member state to maintain a registry of multimodal transport operators, or MTOs for short.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: MTOs have the option to join the registry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: For these MTOs, LTA will issue them with registration certificates, after assessing that they have met requirements such as having insurance to cover any payment of claims, and maintaining a minimum level of assets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Competent National Body can also cancel the registration of MTOs if they have falsified material or contravened conditions of the certificate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The second area of the Bill relates to the Multimodal Transport Document.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It will serve as a common documentational framework to be issued by MTOs registered with a Competent National Body.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: MTOs will be able to issue this document to consignors, which are the parties engaging the MTOs for the conveyance of the goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This document will be recognised by all ASEAN member states to certify that the MTO has taken charge of the goods and will deliver them in accordance with the multimodal transport contract.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Third, the Bill establishes a legal framework on the liabilities of the MTOs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Today, when disputes occur, liability between operators and consignors will be determined based on their contract terms, common law or other legislation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: With the Bill, there will be minimum standards for the liability regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: For example, MTOs will be liable for the loss of, damage to, or delay in the delivery of goods when the goods are in their charge, but they will not be liable if these are due to inherent defects or caused by parties handing over the goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Fourth, the Bill also lays out the roles and responsibilities of the consignors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Consignors are required to accurately inform the operators of the details of the goods that they will be carrying, including if the goods to be transported are deemed dangerous in accordance to domestic laws or international conventions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: If they fail to do so, they will be liable for any losses incurred related to such goods.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Harmonised regional and global transport environments encourage global trade and tourism to flourish.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The various elements of transport are akin to cogs in the wheel of a massive machinery.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If one part gets stuck, the rest of the machinery will not be able to move smoothly.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We saw how this came into play during the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Border restrictions and closures worldwide caused supply chain disruptions in almost every country.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Our excellent relationships and various bilateral agreements established with our foreign counterparts over the years enabled us to facilitate border movements for the transport of essential goods and services.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Today, countries looking to diversify their supply chains have set their sights on ASEAN, so we will certainly see a greater movement of goods and services within the region.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Moreover, in the past decade, the ASEAN region has exhibited strong economic growth, which is driven by rapid urbanisation.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: A burgeoning middle-class population translates into increased spending power, providing viable markets of consumers in the region for our local companies to appeal to.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The logistics sector in Singapore has grown with the rise of e-commerce.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The AFAMT framework has been described as useful for new logistics entrants to gain a foothold in new ASEAN markets.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I believe that this would mean the threshold for eligibility is not out of reach for the less established logistics companies.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: At the same time, we must also ensure that there is a robust system in place to prevent the movement of illicit goods, such as drugs, weapons, wildlife and so on.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will there be outreach efforts to encourage companies to join the registry for example?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Specifically, how would being on the registry or possessing a Multimodal Transport Document improve their access to potential clients in the ASEAN region?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will they enjoy some form of protection and insurance for their services and goods?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Among the many challenges associated with overseas operations, one of the major concerns is making sense of the foreign policies and laws.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If their cargo or carriers go missing or get seized, would they receive assistance to retrieve it?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With extreme weather causing more catastrophic events and natural disasters, do they get some form of insurance or support as part of the registry to curb their losses?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This could take the form of strategic planning and risk management to help them navigate the safest routes based on the season and current trends.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The current COVID-19 pandemic has emphasised the importance of transport network to ensure that essential items from food to medicine can be moved expeditiously, with minimum hinderance.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I believe that being part of this registry can only be a boon.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Administrative work, red tape and long waiting times are costly aspects of business overheads.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It streamlines the process such that companies seeking to transport goods across ASEAN would not have to navigate different regulations.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This would translate into lower overheads and better margins for companies.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Reduced logistics means and presents a win-win situation for all.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: May it be a stepping stone for our logistics sector to soar to greater heights.

text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.25 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A strong logistics hub is the backbone of trade.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Minister Iswaran said at the launch of the Logistics Industry Transformation Map (ITM) in 2016, "logistics is a critical enabler of our economy and our everyday lives".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore has fared well in the past few years, placing seventh in the world and second in ASEAN in the World Bank's 2018 Logistics Performance Index.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: More recently, Singapore's strength in logistics has also put it in good stead to become a COVID-19 vaccine distribution hub for the region.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first area of clarification is on the registration regime set out for the Singapore Competent National Body.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The process of appealing decisions made by the Competent National Body would benefit from clarity in two respects.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, will a holder of a registration certificate be able to appeal the Competent National Body's decision to add to, vary or revoke any of the conditions of a registration certificate?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, rather than the Competent National Body state in writing the reasons for refusal to issue or renew a registration certificate only if requested by the applicant, can the Ministry consider making known the reasons for refusal upfront?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Providing reasons for refusal to issue or renew a registration certificate upfront would avoid unnecessary back-and-forth and save everyone some time and effort.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second area of clarification is on environmental sustainability.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Ministry share how Singapore's AFAMT National Work Plan aims to achieve this goal?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The reason I am asking is that a region-wide strategic alignment on transport and logistics is a great opportunity to coordinate ASEAN and Singapore's plans for sustainability.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In 2019, the European Commission released a report, titled "Transport in the European Union: Current Trends and Issues".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The report provides an array of recommendations on how the EU member states can align the development of their multimodal transport network in an environmentally sustainable way.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One recommendation is to impose environmentally differentiated port charges to stimulate investment in green vessels.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will the Ministry work with regional partners to study such initiatives?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This can foster the longer term development of sustainable transport infrastructure in ASEAN and advance Singapore's status as a global logistics hub.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am sure that logistics companies in Singapore will welcome the convenience this new framework provides.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Our SMEs which sell to other countries will also benefit from it.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The reduced red tape will lower administrative costs and processing time, facilitate businesses within ASEAN and foster new partnership explorations.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In English): Would the Minister elaborate on the criteria to be admitted into the registry?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In addition, how does a customer know the amount of liability insurance that a multimodal transport provider has purchased?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The amount of contracts that it can undertake should be predicated on the amount of liability insurance it has subscribed to.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I also have a concern regarding the language of the transport documentation.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In the past, our companies had to coordinate the various modes of transportation, including ship and railway.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Railway receipts and delivery notes issued by overseas service providers are not stated in English and thus cannot be submitted to financiers in Singapore as proof of delivery unless these documents are translated and signed off by notary public.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The multimodal transport document should follow International Chamber of Commerce Banking rules and be accepted by banks in the event the consignor or consignee requires financing.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This important piece of document proves that shipment has been made.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: ASEAN is an important gateway to other parts of Asia.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Thus, I hope that we will have a common language for all related supporting transport documents.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am also hopeful that this new framework will create more advanced jobs in the logistics sector.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: A multimodal transport operator's most important asset is its staff who must be well-versed in international transport procedures and regulations.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In Singapore, the vocational training courses offered by the Singapore Logistics Association are excellent.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But each MTO should take the responsibility to continuously train their staff by providing in-house or on-the-job training.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The new connectivity will boost supply chain efficiency and help to cement Singapore’s status as a trade, logistics and connectivity hub.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Good connectivity in turn complement the various Free Trade Agreements which Singapore and ASEAN have inked with other regions and countries.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I support the Bill as it will elevate our logistics industry and solidify Singapore’s position as the top logistics hub in Asia, if not the world.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It must be a company or a person whose business name is registered in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It must also have a principal place of business in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It needs to have an insurance, bond, guarantee or other financial arrangements that can cover payment for claims arising from any loss, damage or delay in the delivery of the goods.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Lastly, the company must maintain the prescribed minimum assets.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These criteria are reasonable and would not be entry barriers for logistics companies.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If the House approves this Bill, we will work with industry associations to reach out to logistics companies during the implementation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If there are any appeals from the companies, these can be submitted to the Minister for consideration.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This can help potential customers make informed decisions before engaging logistics companies for their multimodal transport services.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The ASEAN Framework Agreement on Multimodal Transport does not introduce additional requirements on the type of goods or materials that can be transported.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: However, the Bill requires the consignor to accurately inform the multimodal transport operator, or MTO for short, of the nature of the goods.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In particular, the consignor will need to spell out if any of its goods are of dangerous character, and could endanger life or property.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If it fails to do so, the consignor will be liable to the MTO, if the MTO incurs any loss during the shipment that is due to the dangerous nature of the goods.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To protect logistics companies, the Bill also sets out exclusion conditions to exempt MTOs from liability in the event of loss or damage to goods due to unforeseen conditions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Don Wee suggested that the contents of the Multimodal Transport Document be specified in English, to lower transaction costs for businesses.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The ASEAN Framework Agreement on Multimodal Transport does not explicitly state the language requirements of the Multimodal Transport Document.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: However, as English is the official working language of ASEAN, we will work with fellow ASEAN member states towards formalising this arrangement for the implementation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There have been precedents in other ASEAN initiatives where documents are required to be in English or to be accompanied by a certified English translation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Lastly, Mr Louis Ng asked about environmental sustainability for transport.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The ASEAN Framework Agreement on Multimodal Transport is focused on the legal, regulatory and procedural aspects of facilitating the multimodal transport of goods across ASEAN member states.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, it does not deal with environmental sustainability issues per se.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Having said that, ASEAN recognises the importance of environmental sustainability including in the area of transport, and there are other ASEAN initiatives and platforms that promote this goal.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And Singapore, we are involved in these initiatives.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These include the ASEAN Regional Strategy on Sustainable Land Transport, which was adopted by ASEAN Transport Ministers in 2018.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Another example is the ASEAN Green Ship Strategy which was adopted in 2019.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Together with the ASEAN Framework Agreement on the Facilitation of Goods in Transit and the ASEAN Framework Agreement on the Facilitation of Inter-State Transport that Singapore have already ratified, this will bring us one step closer towards the goal of enhancing regional integration, which Members have spoken about.
